title: Thermal Time
text: Thermal time one commonly used concepts crop modelling. widely used describe crop development phenology forms basis many APSIM crop models. apsimwise ecosystem provides consistent interface calculating thermal time across multiple crops maintaining crop-specific algorithms default parameter values. vignette explains design philosophy demonstrates different apsimwise packages work together.

title: Thermal Time
text: apsimwise ecosystem separates calculation thermal times three layers: apsimwise user facing interface rapsimng.* crop specific parameters tidyweather generic thermal time functions     separation three goals: Avoid duplicating generic calculations. Keep crop-specific knowledge close crop package. Provide simple user-facing interface. weather data APSIM format read using read_weather() tidyweather package. tidyweather package contains weather-related calculations independent crop type. daily thermal time calculated using thermal_time() function specified temperature response parameters (e.g. three cardinal temperatures) using tidyverse syntax. Three methods available calculating daily thermal time: Daily mean temperature Three-hourly estimates air temperature Hourly estimates air temperature interpolating daily maximum minimum temperatures using sinusoidal method sunlight hours exponential decline nighttime hours Daily mean temperature simplest method suitable applications. Method 3hr uses three-hourly estimates air temperature calculate thermal time. Method HourlySinPpAdjusted uses hourly estimates air temperature calculate thermal time requires date latitude. Argument latitude requires single value weather record. case multiple weather records, group_by(name) can used ensure first latitude value used weather record. Figure 1 tidyweather package contain crop-specific parameters. Crop-specific packages provide thermal time related parameter values individual crops match crop configuration APSIM NG including: rapsimng.wheat rapsimng.canola rapsimng.chickpea rapsimng.lentil rapsimng.lupin rapsimng.fababean crop parameters can accessed using crop() function directly crop package. crop-specific thermal times calculated using thermal_time() function package. following examples demonstrate calculate thermal time wheat, lupin, canola using crop-specific packages. Wheat uses three hourly method calculate thermal time. Lupin uses hourly method calculate thermal time requires date latitude. Argument latitude requires single value weather record. case multiple weather records, group_by(name) can used ensure first latitude value used weather record. Canola also uses three hourly method different cardinal temperatures calculate thermal time. Figure 2 apsimwise package provides unified interface users. Instead remembering package contains function, users can work common API. thermal times calculated using thermal_time() function apsimwise package wheat, lupin, canola. Figure 3 apsimwise automatically dispatches calculation appropriate crop package preserving crop-specific defaults.

title: Thermal Time
text: tidyweather package contains weather-related calculations independent crop type. daily thermal time calculated using thermal_time() function specified temperature response parameters (e.g. three cardinal temperatures) using tidyverse syntax. Three methods available calculating daily thermal time: Daily mean temperature Three-hourly estimates air temperature Hourly estimates air temperature interpolating daily maximum minimum temperatures using sinusoidal method sunlight hours exponential decline nighttime hours Daily mean temperature simplest method suitable applications. Method 3hr uses three-hourly estimates air temperature calculate thermal time. Method HourlySinPpAdjusted uses hourly estimates air temperature calculate thermal time requires date latitude. Argument latitude requires single value weather record. case multiple weather records, group_by(name) can used ensure first latitude value used weather record. Figure 1 tidyweather package contain crop-specific parameters.
code: tt_mean <- records |>     mutate(         tt = tidyweather::thermal_time(             mint = mint,             maxt = maxt,             x_temp = c(0, 26, 37),             y_temp = c(0, 26, 0)         )     ) |>     mutate(method = "mean") tt_3hour <- records |>     mutate(         tt = tidyweather::thermal_time(             mint = mint,             maxt = maxt,             x_temp = c(0, 26, 37),             y_temp = c(0, 26, 0),             method = "3hr"         )     ) |>     mutate(method = "3hr") tt_hourly <- records |>     group_by(name) |>     mutate(         tt = tidyweather::thermal_time(             mint = mint,             maxt = maxt,             x_temp = c(0, 26, 37),             y_temp = c(0, 26, 0),             date = date,             latitude = latitude[1],             method = "HourlySinPpAdjusted"         )     ) |>     mutate(method = "hourly") tt_all <- bind_rows(tt_mean, tt_3hour, tt_hourly) tt_all |>     ggplot() +     geom_point(aes(x = date, y = tt)) +     theme_bw() +     facet_grid(method~name)

code: library(apsimwise) # Example weather data mint <- c(0, 10) maxt <- c(30, 40) date <- as.Date(c("2024-01-01", "2024-01-02"))  # Use default lupin parameters thermal_time(   mint,   maxt,   date = date,   lat = -27,   crop = "lupin" ) #> [1] 16.64386 24.88400  # Modify the global lupin thermal time response for all following calculations crop("lupin")$set(   "phenology.thermal_time" =   list(     x = c(0, 25, 35),     y = c(0, 25, 0)   ) ) thermal_time(   mint,   maxt,   date = date,   lat = -27,   crop = "lupin" ) #> [1] 16.64386 24.88400  #
